question: Which of the following antitussive can lead to hallucinations
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Morphine" -> "opioid receptor activation" -> "central nervous system effects" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Diphenhydramine" -> "anticholinergic effects" -> "central nervous system effects" -> "possible hallucinations" -> 60%
analysis: Dextromethorphan is an antitussive that acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist, which can lead to altered neurotransmission and is known to cause hallucinations, especially at higher doses. This is a well-documented side effect and aligns with the pharmacological action of dextromethorphan. While morphine can also cause hallucinations due to its effects on the central nervous system, it is primarily an opioid analgesic, and hallucinations are not its primary side effect. Diphenhydramine, an antihistamine, can cause central nervous system effects, including hallucinations, but this is less common and not its primary action. Aprepitant is not typically associated with hallucinations. Therefore, based on the pharmacological profile and consensus, dextromethorphan is the most likely antitussive to lead to hallucinations.
